detail.longDescription: Inflated Titles, Inflated Egos: Narcissism Predicts the Desire for Public Rewards "Specifically, people higher (vs. lower) in narcissism were more motivated by public rewards in their workplaces, more likely to prefer public versions of the same rewards, and more likely to accept a job with a better title rather than higher pay." Zitek, E. M., Krause, V., & Jordan, A. H. (2026). Inflated Titles, Inflated Egos: Narcissism Predicts the Desire for Public Rewards. Social Psychological and Personality Science, 0(0). https:// doi.org/10.1177/19485506261486 505 # OpenAccess # OA # Academia # Research # Article # Narcissism # Psychology # Jobs
